To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the transnational aid and assistance that is being directed at civil society development in Bosnia-Herzgovina is not leading to the creation of a ‘north’ and ‘south’ dichotomy, but rather is contributing to the creation of new forms of environmentalism that are unique to post-conflict societies in the former Yugoslavia.

1) transnational aid has not led to a replication of west European environmental movement forms and practices in Bosnia-Herzgovina; 2) transnational aid is not a sufficient condition for the development of civil society in Bosnia-Herzeogovina.

the structural context of post-conflict Bosnia has a profound impact on environmental movement behaviour and that the environment is not a ‘universal’ cause that transcends political divisions and social differences.
In summary, our research is concerned with

how environmental politics and environmental movements in post-conflict societies differ from their counterparts in established liberal democracies, and how the environment and civil societies in post-socialist and post-conflict countries are being transformed by the impact of trans-national donor assistance and the transfer of environmental expertise.

how the environmental movements and civil society in a post-conflict society are shaped by the legacies of the conflict and the post-conflict political structures, as well as the impact of external donor assistance.

the ways in which environmental movements in the post-socialist and post-conflict contexts are shaped and constrained by the political and social contexts in which they operate, as well as the extent to which they are able to develop and sustain a distinctive identity and agenda.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, in Bosnia-Herzogovina, transnational assistance is having an impact, but that this is neither as positive nor as negative as might have been predicted by those who assume that the ‘North-South divide’ is being overcome by the ‘globalisation of environmental politics’.

environmental movements in post-conflict societies are more likely to be shaped by the legacies of conflict and the structural context in which they are located, rather than by the influence of transnational donors.
the environment and civil societies in post-conflict societies are neither north nor south, but rather a unique combination of both.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the environment and civil societies in Bosnia are not simply ‘north’ or ‘south’, but rather, are situated in an intermediary position between these two poles.

we found a strong correlation between the degree to which the environment has been politicised and the degree to which it has been depoliticised, and that these two processes were in turn strongly correlated with each other.
the environmental movement in Bosnia is still in a state of flux.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the environment and civil societies in post-conflict countries are neither ‘north’ nor ’south’ but rather a unique combination of local, national and transnational influences.
the environmental movement in post-conflict societies is not necessarily on course for convergence with its Northern counterparts.
environmental non-governmental organizations are not simply ‘north’ or ‘south’, but rather are situated within a specific set of political, economic and historical circumstances.
